## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Jhānantarikakathā* (Kv 18.7) is a doctrinal controversy preserved in the eighteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text examines the proposition that there exist intermediate stages between meditative absorptions (*jhānantarika*) [Bareau 1955; Dube 1980]. André Bareau records this thesis as maintained by branches of the Andhakas, who affirmed intermediate meditative states between consecutive *jhānas* [Bareau 1955]. S. N. Dube observes that the advocacy of *jhānantarika* is attributed to the Sammatīyas in counterpoint to the thesis of *jhāna-saṅkamati*, and notes that the commentator Buddhaghosa explicitly distinguished this sectarian view from the orthodox Theravāda fivefold *jhāna* scheme [Dube 1980].
SuttaCentral records one translation in one language and cross-references the topic to the *Dasuttara Sutta* (DN 34) and the *Vitakkānupatitakathā* (Kv 9.7) [SuttaCentral]. Machine analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 788 text-reuse matches between this controversy and 51 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse occurs with the *Vitakkattika* of the Paṭṭhāna (Patthana 1.7), disciplinary rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (Pārājika 4 and Pācittiya 8), and related Kathāvatthu chapters, including Kv 9.7, Kv 8.2 (*Antarābhavakathā*), Kv 5.4 (*Niyāmakathā*), and the immediately preceding section Kv 18.6 (*Jhānasaṅkantikathā*) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (Ds 2.1.2), the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128), the *Asaṅkhata Saṁyutta* (SN 43), the *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), and several Abhidhamma commentaries (*Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus].
